alt: Cleaned concrete pool patio beside a brick home

problems: The green algae and black dirt on the concrete look painted on. The patches are saturated neon green and the black areas are heavy and uniform.
The dark streaks look like cast shadows but don't match the lighting in the rest of the scene. The sky is overcast, so there should be no hard shadows.
The dirt covers the flagstone border strip and the left patio edge in a smeared, inconsistent way. It looks like an overlay, not real grime.
The dirt pattern doesn't follow the surface texture or seams of the concrete.
The dirt looks unnaturally severe for the same slab shown clean in B, so a homeowner would likely see it as exaggerated or fake.
The geometry, objects, hose and furniture match B. The only change is the surface dirt.
The 'dirt' on the patio looks like spilled black soil or tar with neon-green paint-like patches. It doesn't look like real grime, algae or mildew on a pool deck.
The staining is unrealistically heavy and high-contrast, with sharp, blotchy edges. It looks painted on, not like gradual weathering.
A has an extra black hose or cable line in the lower middle, running from about (410,460) to (540,688). B doesn't have it, so something was added beyond the surface change.
A has small puddle or reflection patches near the top of the stained area that B doesn't show.
Black dirt specks were added on the left deck near the chair and side table. They look scattered, not natural.
The camera angle and the other objects match B, including the chair, pool, umbrella, stone wall and plants.
